why: THE CEILING IS WHERE THE FILE STANDS, NOT WHERE mg-ea0e AIMED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE. mg-ea0e's target was under 6,000 words and it landed at 4,658 on 2026-08-06. STATE.md is 19,077 words at this commit. Setting this number to 6,000 would make the gate RED ON ARRIVAL by 13,077 words and block every merge in this repository from the moment it landed, for a reason no author of an unrelated branch could act on — the exact construction code/control_gate_724a/gate.py refuses in its own docstring about a different suite, and the exact way a control gets deleted or suppressed within a week (mg-d91f). A ratchet is not a target: it is a monotone floor under a regression, and it binds from wherever it is set. 6,000 words is NOT withdrawn — it remains what mg-ea0e aimed at and what docs/state-history/ was built to make reachable, and code/state_ratchet_e331/out_p1_growth.txt §3 measures the gap as a DEBT of 13,077 words with a named remedy (5 attempt-index rows totalling 7,351 words that belong in docs/state-history/attempt-*.md, where 9 of their siblings already live). tighten_below is 500 words under the ceiling — about 2.6% of the file — so that ordinary editing does not demand a config change, while any landing that actually pays down the debt is forced to bank it here in the same commit. Banking is the half that makes this a ratchet rather than a cap: mg-34bf cut 28,321 bytes on 2026-07-30 and was 78% undone in 8.5 hours; mg-ea0e cut 153,938 bytes on 2026-08-06 and was 59% undone in 95 hours. Both cuts were real work. Neither was banked, so neither held. RAISED FROM 18,969 TO 19,077 IN THE COMMIT THAT CAUSED IT, which is the procedure this file documents, exercised by its own author on the first landing that needed it: mg-e331 adds one paragraph to STATE.md pointing readers at this ceiling, worth 108 words. Those words could NOT live in docs/state-history/ — a pointer to the constraint is only discoverable at the site the constraint applies to, which is the whole reason it is there. This raise is what the mechanism looks like working: the growth is 108 words, it is declared, and the reason is written down.
how_to_change_this: Two one-line edits and both belong IN THE COMMIT THAT CAUSES THEM, never in a later cleanup. GROWING: move words_ceiling up, set set_at_words to the same number, and append a sentence to why saying what the words are and why they could not live in docs/state-history/. SHRINKING past tighten_below: move words_ceiling DOWN to what you achieved and set tighten_below to 500 under it. There is no --refresh mode and there will not be one: a ratchet that rewrites its own threshold on demand is laundering with extra steps.
